description.narrative:
The proposed project, Strengthening Humanitarian Safety, aims to enhance the ability of humanitarian organisations to operate safely in high-risk environments by delivering integrated safety services, data, and policy support aligned with INSO’s global program strategy. The project will support nearly 1400 NGO partners with analysis, training, advisory services, and evidence-based decision-making. INSO is requesting 4.000.000 EUR (2.000.000 EUR/ per fiscal year) from the German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) to implement this project over an 18-month period from 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2027.
This project is particularly critical at the onset of the humanitarian “reset”, growing hyper‑prioritisation of needs and increasing access constraints, as these create clear gaps in safety coordination and operational support. As international coordination capacities contract in key contexts, INSO will build on its role as a central NGO safety platform to sustain and adapt support where it is most needed. Leveraging its presence across 20+ high-risk settings, INSO will equip partner organisations to adopt more systematic, risk-informed planning and decision-making practices, thereby improving the continuity, reach, and security of programme delivery.
The project will strengthen safe humanitarian access and enable partners to sustain operations in high-risk environments by delivering timely alerts, rigorous contextual analysis, targeted training, and structured coordination at country, regional, and global levels. The project will focus on implementation through INSO global programming, and the priority contexts—Afghanistan, Central African Republic, Chad, Palestine, South Sudan, and Colombia—where acute access and security constraints require sustained, high-quality operational support.

sector.narrative: INSO provides a range of support services to non-profit humanitarian organisations including crisis support and coordination, capacity building, training information management, analysis advice, etc.
